You are working in the Trueup repository (this folder). Foreground only. Do not commit, push or post. Never print a key. Take up to 30 minutes; careful beats fast. Work carefully: keep every number and fact exactly; change words, not facts.

Goal: remove internal words, internal notes and weakness-first phrasing from everything a judge reads.

1. Delete these internal files with `git rm`: docs/owner-actions.md, docs/posts.md, docs/video-script.md. Remove any links to them (grep the repo: README.md, docs/*, live/static/*, hackathon.md). If a test reads one of them, update that test to stop reading it (never weaken a number check).

2. Plain words on the site pages (live/static/index.html, demo.html, how-it-works.html, fixes.html, built-with.html, and the generator live/build_fixes.py which writes fixes.html; run it after) and in README.md and docs/getting-started.md, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/built-with.md, docs/limits.md, docs/witness-before-after.md, docs/neatlogs-email.md, docs/business-plan.md. Visible text only (never break HTML tags, code, file paths, URLs, or code identifiers like `instrumentations=[...]`). Replace:
   - "upstream" -> "to the companies that make these tools" / "sent to Arize, Traceloop and neatlogs" (as fits); "Sent upstream" tag -> "Sent"
   - "planner, checker, fixer, verifier" -> describe what they do: "the part that plans tests", "the part that checks results", "the part that writes fixes", "the part that proves fixes" (or "plans tests, checks results, writes and proves fixes")
   - "checker" alone -> "Trueup's checks"; "verifier" -> "the proof step"; "withdrawn" -> "set aside"; "sweep" -> "full run of all 57 test failures"; "root span" quote -> say Arize's head of open source said fixing it was "the right goal"
   - "instrumentation" in prose -> "tracing code"; "leads" meaning possible problems -> "possible problems" ("engineering leads" meaning people is fine)
   - "scenario(s)" in prose -> "test case(s)" or "plan(s)" for cfo.ai scenarios -> "cases"
   - "observed"/"reported" as audit labels -> drop
   Keep product names: Trueup Witness, TRACE DISAGREE, neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai, Arize, Traceloop, OpenInference, OpenLLMetry, and neatlogs detection names quoted exactly as they are named in neatlogs (e.g. "Trueup: lead withdrawn (own false alarm)") because those are real names.

3. Weakness-first phrasing: in the files above, any sentence that leads with a failure or "not done" should lead with what works, keeping the honest fact after it. Example: "Our first attempt stayed 2 → 2" -> keep, but only after the 2 → 0 result and framed as "how we got there".

4. hackathon.md is the dated build log; do NOT rewrite its history. But:
   - Add at the very top, under the title, a short "Read this first" block (5-7 plain lines): what Trueup is, the 2 → 0 live result with 0 false alarms in 40 calls, the neatlogs email finding, the three pull requests (links), the live demo link, and one line: "Below is the dated build log, kept as written, including the mistakes and how we fixed them."
   - Rephrase lines that start with "Not done" into "Left for later:" with the same facts.
   - Remove the audit labels OBSERVED / DOCUMENTED / REPORTED / ASSUMED from the log (keep the sentences), but keep heading anchors working: the README links `hackathon.md#what-entire-recorded-and-what-it-did-not-12-oct-observed`; if you change that heading, update the README link to the new anchor.

5. Run `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run trueup bundle && uv run trueup verify` until green. Print: files changed, files deleted, any test you changed and why, and a list of any banned word still present in visible text with its reason.

6. Entire wording. The hackathon rule only asked us to give the coding agent context through Entire checkpoints or the entire-graph, with checkpoints as evidence. It never asked for every commit to be recorded. So nothing here is a mistake and must not be called one. Never write "mistake", "gap", "unrecorded", "did not record" or "no Entire record" about Entire anywhere a judge reads. Never claim every commit was recorded, and never invent or change a number.
   - README.md: delete the whole bullet that starts `- **[Our mistake with Entire]`. Keep the Entire bullet above it.
   - hackathon.md: replace the section "## What Entire recorded, and what it did not (12 Oct, OBSERVED)" (heading plus its two paragraphs) with "## What Entire recorded" and one positive paragraph: Entire recorded the core build (the test lab, comparer, checks, test planning, the part that wrote and proved the first fixes, the code-graph step that located them) and later the live app's safety tests, the links from each fix to its record, the product site and the README. Give the number of commits that carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, counted with `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)' | grep -c .` (state it as "N commits carry an Entire record"), and link https://entire.io/gh/Jennycruzy/trueup. Also grep hackathon.md for any other sentence saying work had no Entire record and rephrase it positively or drop it, without changing other facts.
   - docs/built-with.md: replace the "**What Entire did not record.**" paragraph with a short "**What Entire recorded.**" paragraph in the same positive style (same count, link to the build log). In the "Every fix links to the session that made it" paragraph, change "Three of the five fixes have an Entire record; the other two say plainly that their commit has none (see below)." to "Three of the five fixes link to their Entire record."
   - Same changes on live/static/built-with.html (and any other site page) if the text appears there.
   - Finally grep the whole repo (excluding .venv, .trueup and fixes/*/PROVENANCE.md) for: "Our mistake", "what-entire-recorded-and-what-it-did-not", "did not record", "unrecorded", "no Entire record". Fix any link to the old anchor; report every remaining hit.
I'll start by surveying the repo and the files involved.

1	# Trueup Witness
2	
3	**Your dashboard said OK. Your agent crashed.** Trueup Witness checks your AI agent's records against what really happened, warns you inside neatlogs when they disagree, and fixes the tracing code that got it wrong.
4	
5	### Why it matters
6	
7	- **Proven live with real Claude calls:** 2 wrong records before Trueup's fixes, 0 after, and 0 false alarms in 40 normal calls.
8	- **neatlogs' own daily email said 6.2%** of our test runs failed; really 11.1% had crashed (test runs we crashed on purpose).
9	- **The fix we sent Arize was reviewed by their head of open source**, and neatlogs runs that same code for agents, so one fix repairs both.
10	- **Built with all three tools:** neatlogs recorded every run and caught our own agent's mistakes, Entire recorded how Trueup and its fixes were built, cfo.ai built the business plan from measured costs.

36	
37	## Install
38	
39	Python 3.12 or newer.
40	
41	```
42	git clone https://github.com/Jennycruzy/trueup && pip install ./trueup
43	```
44	
45	## Quick start
46	
47	```python
48	import os
49	
50	import trueup.witness
51	trueup.witness.watch()          # once, at start-up, before neatlogs.init()
52	
53	import neatlogs
54	neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], instrumentations=["openai"])
55	
56	with trueup.witness.run("order-1042") as run:   # one job your agent does
57	    answer = agent.handle(order_id="1042")      # your own agent call
58	
59	print(run.disagreements)        # [] when the record matches what really happened
60	```
61	
62	When the record is wrong, Witness adds a red `TRACE DISAGREE` step to that record. It never breaks your app. `TRUEUP_WITNESS=0` turns it off.
63	
64	From the project folder:
65	
66	```
67	uv run entire trueup --help                               # Trueup as an Entire command (needs the Entire CLI)
68	uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library neatlogs  # check your own script safely
69	```
70	
71	## How it works
72	
73	1. Witness reads each AI call off the connection: did the call fail, did the reply finish.
74	2. It compares that with the step neatlogs recorded and flags any mismatch with `TRACE DISAGREE`.
75	3. Trueup's test lab finds the faulty tracing code, writes a fix and proves it.

18	## Quick start
19	
20	Call `watch()` once at start-up, before `neatlogs.init()`. Then wrap each unit of work in `run()`.
21	
22	```python
23	import os
24	
25	import trueup.witness
26	trueup.witness.watch()          # once, at start-up, before neatlogs.init()
27	
28	import neatlogs
29	neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], instrumentations=["openai"])
30	
31	with neatlogs.trace(name="shop-agent", kind="AGENT"):
32	    try:
33	        with trueup.witness.run("order-1042") as run:   # one unit of work
34	            answer = agent.handle(order_id="1042")
35	    except Exception:
36	        pass                    # your app's own error handling; Witness never swallows an error
37	
38	print(run.disagreements)        # [] when the record matches what really happened
39	print(run.notes)                # smaller gaps that do not turn the light on
40	```
41	
42	- `run()` gives you the run as soon as it starts. `run.disagreements` and `run.notes` are filled in when the
43	  `with` block ends, including when your code raised.
44	- Each disagreement is a small dictionary: `field` (what was compared), `record` (what neatlogs recorded),
45	  `really` (what really happened) and, when Trueup knows the cause, `finding` (the matching Trueup finding).
46	- Witness never changes what your app sends or receives, and if Witness itself fails, your app carries on.
47	
48	## Reading the TRACE DISAGREE step in neatlogs
49	
50	When the record and reality disagree, Witness adds a red step named `TRACE DISAGREE` to the same neatlogs record,
51	next to the step that is wrong. Its fields say what was compared:
52	
53	| field | meaning |
54	|---|---|
55	| `call_status` | One AI call: neatlogs says SUCCESS (or ERROR), but the call really failed (or succeeded). |
56	| `run_status` | The whole run: your code raised, but every top step in the record says SUCCESS. |
57	| `refusal` | The AI refused, but the refusal is missing from the record. |
58	| `tools` | The AI asked for tools, but the record names different tools or none. |
59	
60	A missing AI step (the call happened, the record has no step for it) is also reported, with `record` set to
61	`missing`.
62	
63	## The neatlogs detection to create
64	
65	So that you hear about a disagreement without opening each record:
66	
67	1. In neatlogs, open **Detections** and create a conditional detection that matches steps named
68	   `TRACE DISAGREE`. Call it `TRACE DISAGREE light`.
69	2. Open **Alerts** and add a rule for that detection: at least one occurrence. Pick where it should notify you.

1	# How it works
2	
3	Trueup has two parts. **Witness** runs inside your app and turns on a light when the record is wrong. **The lab**
4	runs on a developer's machine, finds out why the record is wrong, and writes and proves the fix.
5	
6	## Witness
7	
8	### What it reads
9	
10	`watch()` hooks into httpx, the HTTP library that the OpenAI and Anthropic Python SDKs use to talk to their
11	servers. Inside a `run()`, for every call to a chat, responses or messages address, it notes:
12	
13	- the HTTP status and any connection error;
14	- for streamed replies, whether the stream reached its proper end (`[DONE]`, `message_stop` or
15	  `response.completed`) or was cut off, and whether the server sent an error event part-way;
16	- refusals and the names of the tools the AI asked for.
17	
18	Bytes pass straight through to your app unchanged. The added time per call was 2.9005 microseconds at the
19	median (4.809 at most) in the live run.
20	
21	### What it compares
22	
23	`watch()` also attaches a listener to neatlogs, so every step neatlogs records during a `run()` is copied to
24	Witness as well. When the run ends, Witness lines up each real AI call with the matching AI step in the record and
25	asks:
26	
27	1. **Did it fail?** The call failed (error status, connection error, error event, or a cut stream) but the step
28	   says SUCCESS, or the other way round.
29	2. **Did the whole run fail?** Your code raised, but every top step in the record still says SUCCESS.
30	3. **Refusal and tools.** The AI refused or asked for tools, and the record says something else.
31	4. **Is the step there at all?** A call happened with no AI step for it.
32	
33	### When the light turns on
34	
35	Any "no" above is a **disagreement**: the record says the opposite of what happened. Witness adds a red
36	`TRACE DISAGREE` step to the same neatlogs record and adds the disagreement to `run.disagreements`.
37	
38	### Notes
39	
40	Some gaps are real but do not make the record say the opposite of what happened. Example: the step is correctly
41	marked ERROR but carries no error details. Witness lists these in `run.notes` and leaves the light off. Witness's
42	own `TRACE DISAGREE` steps are never compared, so one wrong record gives one mark, not two.
43	
44	## The lab
45	
46	### Practice AI server
47	
48	A local server that answers like OpenAI (chat and responses) and Anthropic (messages), and fails on purpose:
49	server errors, connections cut mid-reply, error events in a stream, refusals, tool calls, agents that hit their
50	step limit. It keeps its own log of exactly what it sent. Trueup ships 51 of these test cases and runs them
51	against neatlogs, OpenInference (Arize) and OpenLLMetry (Traceloop).
52	
53	### Comparison
54	
55	For each case, Trueup compares what really happened (the server's log and whether the app raised) with what the
56	tracing library recorded. Every difference is a possible problem.
57	
58	### Checker rules
59	
60	A possible problem becomes a confirmed **finding** only if it passes seven rules:
61	
62	1. It happens twice in a row, each time in a fresh process.
63	2. It happens with the library's recommended setup.
64	3. It happens on the latest release and on the library's main branch.
65	4. The practice server really sent what Trueup says it sent.
66	5. The test itself is sound (no shared state, nothing sent anywhere).
67	6. Another library, or the published OpenTelemetry conventions (the shared standard for these records), shows
68	   the right behaviour.
69	7. A script under 40 lines shows it on its own.
70	
71	Anything that fails a rule is set aside with the reason, never deleted. The result so far: 32 confirmed findings
72	across the three libraries.
73	
74	### Fixer
75	
76	For a finding, Trueup clones the library, finds the code most likely at fault, and asks a model for a small
77	change plus one new test. Code, not the model, rejects edits outside the library, in its tests, or that do not
78	compile.
79	
80	### Verifier
81	
82	A fix counts only if:
83	
84	- the new test fails before the change and passes after;
85	- the library's own test suite shows no new failure;
86	- the finding's test cases now match what really happened;
87	- all test cases together show no new difference.
88	
89	Up to three tries per run; a failed try goes back to the model with the reason. Five fixes have passed so far.
90	
91	### Upstream drafts
92	
93	`trueup upstream` writes the issue and pull-request text for a proven fix into `upstream/`. It never posts.
94	A person re-checks the latest release, main and open pull requests, then posts. Three have been posted:
95	[Arize-ai/openinference#4024](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024),
96	[traceloop/openllmetry#4610](https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry/pull/4610) and
97	[neatlogs/neatlogs#207](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/207).
98	
99	### Checking the numbers
100	
101	`uv run trueup verify` recomputes every number above from `evidence/` and checks every file's checksum.
